summary.headline: TTK Prestige Q4 FY26 domestic revenue grew 14.4% and company revenue 12.5%, with operating EBITDA of INR81.7 crore, up 43.8%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was driven by domestic demand, with induction cooktops giving a short-term boost to appliances, and exports constrained by supply chain disruption. Operating EBITDA rose 43.8% to INR81.7 crore and PBT rose 35.9% to INR71.9 crore, though exceptional charges relating to the new Labour Code were incurred. Gross margin expanded despite commodity inflation, which management attributed mainly to inventory management and mix, with the mid-quarter price hike only partly visible. For FY26, company revenue grew 9.6% (domestic 9.8%), operating EBITDA grew 12% and PAT rose about 14% to INR185 crore. Management flagged input cost inflation of about 10% post the West Asia conflict and expects margins to dip during the ongoing investment phase.

segments.name: Kitchenware / cookware and cookers
segments.commentary: Kitchenware grew about 10% in FY26 per management, driven by material-led upgrades (stainless steel, triply, cast iron) and ceramics, which management says are growing 20%+ at industry level. Cookers industry mix is about 50-55% stainless steel versus about 45% aluminium. Kitchenware plants run at 85%+ utilisation.

segments.name: Appliances
segments.commentary: Appliances grew about 10% in FY26 per management, with Q4 lifted by induction cooktop demand driven by a replacement shift during the volatile quarter. Appliance plants run at about 75-80% utilisation; the partner-manufactured model is treated as hybrid in-sourcing.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were a drag in Q4 due to disrupted global supply chains, despite order inflow. Management says the business is maintained, prior growth was 20-22% on a small base, and the domestic market is the priority.

segments.name: Prestige Exclusive stores
segments.commentary: Contribute about 12-15% of business and are growing in double digits; about 700+ stores and about 100 new stores opened. Management described them as a significant growth driver.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin or revenue guidance given; management declined to guide on profitability.

EBITDA margin expected to dip over the next few quarters during investment phase, with recovery to earlier 13-14% margin targeted once investments yield results; investment phase to run about 2 more years.
Price increases taken mid-Q4; partial impact in Q4 and balance in Q1 FY27. Further price hikes described as inevitable, calibrated to market response.
INR200 crore strategic spend over 3 years (started Q4 FY25) and about INR300 crore capital deployment, spread across opex and capex, expected to continue for at least a year or more.
Capex expansion planned over the next 2 years, mainly in cookware and across appliances.
Management said current volatility (geopolitics, supply chain, raw materials) will continue to weigh in the next few quarters.
capex_capacity: Recent investment in triply cookware facility at Karjan; further capex planned over next 2 years, especially cookware and appliances.
INR300 crore capital deployment (capex plus opex) planned alongside INR200 crore strategic spend over 3 years.
Opened new innovation centre for design and appliances; invested further in kitchenware R&D infrastructure.
Kitchenware fully in-sourced; appliances made by exclusive external partners, with quality systems invested in them.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand lifted by induction cooktop adoption and replacement of existing appliances; management called it a tactical short-term opportunity and said some trend continues into Q1 FY27.
Input costs rose about 10% on average post West Asia conflict, with some items up about 15%.
Price increases taken mid-quarter; gross margin gain attributed mainly to inventory management, mix and cost initiatives, not pricing.
New entrants in cookware and small domestic appliances are competing on price and D2C e-commerce spend; management believes the category can absorb this and is not overly worried.
General trade growth attributed to company-specific distribution and hygiene initiatives; channel inventory described as normalised.

qa_highlights.question: What drove gross margin expansion despite commodity inflation, and how much was price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 had little pricing impact; a mid-quarter price hike will flow partly in Q4 and partly in Q1. Gains came from inventory management, higher-margin category mix and manufacturing/sourcing cost initiatives. No quantification of price increase was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of appliance growth of about 20% is from induction cooktops, and will momentum continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not quantify the induction contribution but said appliances grew reasonably even excluding it. Some trend continues into Q1, and induction adoption may last a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the input cost inflation currently?
qa_highlights.answer: Average input cost increase of about 10%, with some areas up about 15%, post the war scenario. Price hikes are inevitable, weighed against demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consulting/strategic expense for FY26 and FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: INR200 crore over 3 years started Q4 FY25, to continue for a few more quarters and taking forms beyond consultants. Management did not give a split for FY26 or FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is general trade growth a trend or new this quarter, and is competition hurting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: General trade growth is attributed to company-specific initiatives on distribution and hygiene. Management said new entrants compete on price and D2C, but the category is growing enough to absorb it; Judge is played separately in the mass segment, and its margins were not compared.

qa_highlights.question: What was advertising spend and what is the FY27 budget?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide FY27 ad budget and FY26 amount, saying normally 5-6% of sales is spent on advertising, sales and promotion.

qa_highlights.question: When will EBITDA margin recover, and is it to pre-investment levels?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a dip in EBITDA margin during the investment phase lasting about 2 more years, then a return to the earlier 13-14% margin as investments yield results.

qa_highlights.question: Did GST-related channel filling shift growth from Q3 to Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said channel inventory is normalised and GST had little impact on Q4 performance.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation of about 10% and rising raw material prices; the mid-quarter price hike only partially reflected in Q4, so Q1 FY27 margins depend on price pass-through and demand response.
EBITDA margin dip during the investment phase (about 2 more years) versus target recovery to 13-14%.
Exports constrained by global supply chain disruption; management is prioritising domestic.
Competitive intensity from new entrants and D2C players in cookware and small appliances, and possible pressure on pricing.
Induction cooktop tailwind may be temporary; management says current quarter's demand spike is tactical.
Opacity on spend split (opex vs capex, advertising budget, strategic spend by year), with management declining to give details.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the domestic franchise, but cautious on the outlook, citing volatility from geopolitics, supply chains and raw materials. Management was evasive on guidance, FY27 ad budget, the spend split, Judge's margin profile and new markets, and the CFO declined several specific questions on competition-sensitive spend.
key_quotes: So overall, the domestic performance of 14.4% and company level 12.5% for the quarter.
So, we do believe in the long term that the category seems to be having a robust demand and is being driven, as in the past, by a very strong replacement cycle in some of our kitchenware categories.
Normally, we spend anywhere between a 5% to 6%. That is the number that we normally spend.
So, I think we would not want to give any guidance on that.
